## Routing Decisions for Chapter 5B Evidence (High-Recall)

---

### U0091 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 91
**Relevance:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0092 (near-term cost impacts, labor market implementation effects)

**Material Evidence:**
- Concrete policy action: 2019 replacement of means-tested social pension with basic pension; 2021 contribution rate increases and minimum pension adjustments
- Specific parameter changes: contribution rates rising from 6.5–10% to 15% by 2030; minimum contribution years reduced from ~25 to 15 (2021), reaching 20 by 2031
- Measured outcomes: minimum pension increased to MEX$45,000/year (20+ years contributions) and MEX$85,000/year (average wage earner); Chile/Colombia/U.S. fee cap benchmark

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains concrete policy actions and quantified outcomes directly bearing on 5B.1 (broad-based prosperity vs rents), 5B.3 (credible fiscal rules), 5B.6 (budget quality), and 5B.8 (distributional incidence across earnings levels)

---

### U0092 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 92
**Relevance:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0091 (reform parameters), U0091/U0092 are coupled

**Material Evidence:**
- Measured outcome: pension spending 1.4% GDP (2000) → 4.0% GDP (2021)
- Implementation finding: adverse labor market effects including early retirement enabling labor force decline among older workers, contribution-rate increase creating labor wedge, employment impact pushing workers to informal sector
- Acknowledged policy tradeoff: near-term expenditure rising amid high spending pressures
- Distributional finding: government subsidies concentrated on low earners under new rules

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains measured outcomes (spending trajectory, labor force participation effects), implementation findings (labor wedge), and distributional results bearing on 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8, and 5B.9 (shock/spending-pressure response)

---

### U0093 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 93
**Relevance:** 5B.1, 5B.4

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0094 (nontariff barrier data), U0095 (customs cooperation specifics)

**Material Evidence:**
- Concrete policy action: Mexico-Central America free trade agreement (signed 2011, implemented 2013) with tariff liberalization across product lines
- Quantified trade flows: Mexico exports 1.7% to Central America (2021); imports 0.6%; Central America exports 5.8% to Mexico; 13.5% of Central American imports from Mexico
- Country-specific data: Nicaragua, Guatemala, Belize >8% export exposure to Mexico; Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras >15% import exposure from Mexico
- Concrete recommendation: further trade integration through converging trade rules, infrastructure, human capital, reducing nontariff barriers, customs cooperation

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains concrete policy action (FTA), quantified trade outcomes, and policy recommendations bearing on 5B.1 (legislative/trade agenda) and 5B.4 (fair competition/trade regulations)

---

### U0094 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 94
**Relevance:** 5B.4

**Material Evidence:**
- Measured nontariff barrier index: Mexico in mid-range; some Central American countries persistently at high restriction levels
- Methodology: Estefania-Flores et al. (2022) IMF Working Paper WP/22/1 measurement of aggregate trade restrictions excluding tariffs
- Concrete policy finding: Mexico-Central America FTA resulted in tariff line liberalization with commitment to further elimination
- Source attribution: WTO 2015 for FTA confirmation

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0093 (FTA context), U0095 (customs cooperation specifics)

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains measured regulatory restrictiveness data, methodology attribution, and implementation findings bearing on 5B.4 (fair regulations for competition/trade/investment)

---

### U0095 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 95
**Relevance:** 5B.4, 5B.7

**Material Evidence:**
- Concrete policy recommendation: replicate U.S. customs cooperation programs/mechanisms at Southern border following 1994 NAFTA model
- Specific implementation areas: coordination, border infrastructure, capacity development, risk management, bottleneck reduction

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0093–U0094 (trade integration context)

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains specific named implementation mechanism (NAFTA 1994 cooperation model) and operational findings bearing on 5B.4 (trade facilitation) and 5B.7 (institutional capacity/evaluation)

---

### U0096 — **EXCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 96
**Exclusion Reason:** Table of contents and cover page for informational annex. Contains no policy actions, measured outcomes, costs, distributional results, implementation findings, methods, qualifications, attribution facts, or contrary findings. Generic administrative listing only.

---

### U0097 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 97
**Relevance:** 5B.3

**Material Evidence:**
- FCL (Flexible Credit Line) arrangements: Nov 2021–Nov 2023, SDR 35,650.80 million, zero drawn; prior FCLs from 2010–2019 all zero drawn
- Financial arrangement history documented: six prior FCL arrangements (2009–2021)
- IMF membership and surveillance adequacy confirmed (Article VIII compliance, SDDS subscription)
- Meeting participants attributed (Finance Secretary, Governor, Labor Secretary, Economy Secretary)

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0098 (technical assistance, exchange arrangements)

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains attributed institutional relationships and financial arrangement data bearing on 5B.3 (credible fiscal/debt/monetary rules and institutional independence)

---

### U0098 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 98
**Relevance:** 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.7

**Material Evidence:**
- Technical assistance attribution: 16 missions 2012–2021 across FAD, STA, MCM covering public assets/liabilities management, fiscal framework, public investment, tax policy/compliance, revenue administration, GFS, balance of payments, pension/health systems
- Exchange arrangement qualification: free-floating peso; free of multiple currency practices and restrictions on current international transactions
- Prior consultation date and publication: November 2021 Executive Board consultation, IMF Country Report No. 20/293

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0097 (FCL context, membership status)

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains attributed institutional capacity-building record and exchange arrangement findings bearing on 5B.2 (qualified professionals/operational independence), 5B.3 (monetary rules), and 5B.7 (reliable information/independent evaluation)

---

### U0099 — **EXCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 99
**Exclusion Reason:** URL link to World Bank page only. Contains no policy actions, measured outcomes, costs, distributional results, implementation findings, methods, qualifications, attribution facts, or contrary findings. Not independently evidence-bearing.

---

### U0100 — **INCLUDE**
**Locator:** page 100
**Relevance:** 5B.7

**Material Evidence:**
- Methodology qualification: national accounts follow 2008 SNA; CPI basket based on 2012–2013 National Survey of Household Expenditure and 2014 Household Income and Expenditure Survey
- Attribution: 2021 Data ROSC mission found national accounts high quality; ROSC mission identified specific data reconciliation needs between Banxico and SHCP
- Implementation finding: quarterly government transactions recorded on cash rather than accrual basis; goods for processing abroad treatment gaps; illegal activities coverage gaps
- Technical assistance findings: three missions on chained GDP volume measures and harmonization of national accounts and government finance statistics

**Adjacent Context Needed:** U0098 (prior technical assistance history)

**Exclusion Reason:** N/A — contains method details (SNA 2008, survey bases), implementation findings (data reconciliation gaps, coverage limitations), and attribution (ROSC mission identification) bearing on 5B.7 (reliable economic information and independent evaluation)
